meta.titre: Sauvetage Animal Rescue • Technical rescue for animals in distress
meta.description: Sauvetage Animal Rescue rescues animals in distress across the Montréal Metropolitan Community: trees, rooftops, sewers, ice. Rescue and technical rescue. Reporting line open at all hours.

accueil.heroTitre:
No one else will go.
We go.
accueil.heroTexte: In trees, on rooftops, down sewers and out on the ice. A team trained in rescue and in technical rescue responds to animals in distress across the Montréal Metropolitan Community.
accueil.sectionsTexte: Four ways in, depending on what brought you here.

signalement.texte: An animal trapped, injured or in danger? Our line is open at all hours.

membre.texte: Thirty dollars a year, spent directly in the field.

recrutement.texte: Five functions, from remote dispatch to technical rescue.

services.texte: Technical rescue, support for municipalities, workshops in schools.

accueil.territoireTexte: Sauvetage Animal Rescue covers the entire Montréal metropolitan community: Montréal, Laval, the Montérégie, the Laurentides and Lanaudière. Four thousand square kilometres where dense neighbourhoods, suburbs, farmland and protected natural areas all meet.
territoirePoints: 4.2 million residents, close to half of Québec's population
Calls at height, on ice, in sewers and in confined spaces
A dispatch team handling every report, day and night
accueil.formationsTitre:
Knowing what to do
in an emergency
accueil.formationsTexte: Our courses are built for pet owners and for anyone who encounters animals at work: police, fire services, businesses and animal care staff. Recognize an emergency, approach without being bitten, act correctly while the vet is still minutes away.
accueil.stagesTitre:
Join the team
for a day
accueil.stagesTexte: Eight straight hours with a team on duty, from the meeting point to the last call of the day. You watch the calls come in, the decisions get made and the animals leave safely. It is the most honest way to understand what we do.
stagesPoints: Saturday or Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.
The same price for one or two people
accueil.interventionsTexte: Every line is a mission closed successfully, published automatically from our operational registry.
accueil.soutienTexte: Everything rests on our members and donors. An annual membership pays directly for travel and equipment.
accueil.benevolesTitre:
Someone has to be
willing to go.
accueil.benevolesTexte: An animal stuck fifteen metres up, at the bottom of a sewer or on ice about to give way is no one’s mandate. Our team is trained, equipped and reachable at any hour, because someone has to go.

pied.droits: Sauvetage Animal Rescue. All rights reserved.

membre.intro: Sauvetage Animal Rescue receives no grants. Every rescue is paid for by its members. Becoming a member funds the fuel, the traps, the ropes and the cages that pull an animal out of trouble.
avantages: A personalized PDF membership card, emailed the moment you pay.
A unique member number and a QR code anyone can verify online.
A member area to download your card again at any time.
Eligibility for the organization's draws and contests.
The certainty that 100% of your dues stay in the field.

equipe.intro: About thirty volunteers from emergency services, the animal world and the general public. They give entire days, often at night and on weekends, to go get animals no one else would go get.
equipe.chaineTexte: From the first call to the shelter door, every link matters as much as the next.
equipe.quiTexte: Firefighters, paramedics, police officers, animal health technicians, climbers, divers, accountants, truck drivers. The team does not recruit a profile, it recruits skills and availability. What brings these people together is not their trade, it is their decision to answer when the phone rings.
equipe.engagementTexte: Continuous training, procedures followed to the letter, and the ability to stay composed in front of an injured animal, a distressed owner or an unstable structure. Nobody climbs a tree on day one. You learn, you shadow, you are assessed, then you are assigned.

fiches.surtitre: What to do, what to avoid
fiches.intro: A cat stuck up a tree, a litter of kittens in an alley, a raccoon in the attic, a bird on the ground. These sheets explain what to do, what never to do, and when to call us.
fiches.ctaTexte: No question is a silly one when an animal is involved. Our reporting line is open at all hours and a dispatcher will walk you through it.
fiches.nonTraduite: This sheet has not been translated yet. It is shown in French.

statistiques.intro: These figures are not entered by hand. They are computed straight from our mission registry, from calls closed with a favourable outcome for the animal.
statistiques.methodeTexte: An operation is counted as soon as a team travels to help an animal, whatever the outcome. A rescue, a capture or a transport to a shelter each count as one operation: in every case, time and resources were committed for that animal. The animal figure adds up the adults and juveniles recorded for each operation.
statistiques.vide: Statistics are unavailable at the moment.
statistiques.note: Data from 1 January to 2 August comes from the mission registry. Data from 3 to 21 August is reconstructed from the dispatch thread. The counters at the top of the page are live.
statistiques.anneeIntro: From 1 January to 21 August 2026. Every number comes from operations actually carried out, recorded one by one.
statistiques.rythmeTexte: Calls peak in summer, when the young leave the nest and people are outdoors. Weekends are busier than weekdays, and nearly half of all operations take place in the evening or at night, when other resources are closed.
statistiques.uniteBarres: Every chart on this page counts call-outs, never animals. One operation for three ducklings counts as one call-out.

signalement.intro: An animal trapped, injured, orphaned or in danger anywhere in the Montréal metropolitan community? Here is how to reach us and what we need to know.
signalement.urgenceTexte: The animal is in distress: in immediate danger, injured, in the water or stuck for several hours. Our reporting team reviews your call and gets back to you as soon as possible, to gather the details needed and, if warranted, dispatch a team.
signalement.formulaireTexte: Fill in the form: your report lands directly in our dispatch queue, with a tracking number.
avantListe: Note the exact address or the nearest landmark.
Keep your distance: a frightened animal bites, scratches and bolts toward danger.
Do not try to get a cat down from a tree yourself.
Do not give milk or food to an injured or dehydrated animal.
Take a photo from a distance if it is safe to do so.
Keep children and other pets away.
signalement.horsTexte: Our team is a technical rescue team for animals. Some situations call for other resources: here is who to contact depending on the case.

hors.question: Animal cruelty or neglect
hors.reponse: MAPAQ reporting line, 1 844 ANIMAUX. The Montreal SPCA also runs a 24 hour animal cruelty reporting line, at 1 855 711-7575.

hors.question: An animal on the highway or roadside
hors.reponse: Dial 511, the Ministère des Transports line. Their patrollers are dispatched and call us in if needed.

hors.question: A dead animal on the roadway
hors.reponse: On a municipal street, contact your municipality's public works. On a numbered route or highway, dial 511.

hors.question: A stray animal, a capture, spay/neuter or adoption
hors.reponse: Contact the animal services covering your municipality. Check your municipality’s website to find out which one serves your area.

hors.question: An injured or dead wild animal under mandatory reporting rules
hors.reponse: Some wildlife species must be reported when found injured or dead. Call the SOS Braconnage wildlife emergency line, at 1 800 463-2191.

distinctions.intro: Our responders receive neither salary nor bonus. What marks their commitment are the honours the organisation awards them, worn on the uniform and entered in their file.
distinctions.aVenirTexte: The Sauvetage Animal Rescue honours system is being developed. Criteria, names and how they are worn on the uniform will be settled before the first honours are awarded. This page will then present each of them.

memoriam.dedicace: An organisation is made of people. This page is dedicated to those who carried Sauvetage Animal Rescue and are no longer with us. Their work continues through every mission.
memoriam.aucun: Tributes are added to this page with the agreement of the family.
memoriam.contact: To propose a tribute, write to the Executive Director at e.dussault@sar.quebec.

serie.intro: A film crew followed our responders on their missions. The result is a documentary series showing the work exactly as it happens.
